Definition: probably to be sleek, i.e. glossy; hence (through the idea of polishing) to excogitate (as if forming in the mind)
BiblicalUsage: This word is used twice, for growing sleek and for thinking upon. Jeremiah says the wicked are waxen fat, they shine, they overpass the deeds of the wicked; and the shipmaster comes to Jonah in the storm and says, arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for sleekness and for thought carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the contrast, that the sleek rich shine while the poor go unjudged, and the heathen sailor begs God to think upon them.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
